changes.before: A lattice vector is $\mathbf r=U\mathbf a+V\mathbf b+W\mathbf c$ with integers $U,V,W$.
changes.after: Vectors $\mathbf r=U\mathbf a+V\mathbf b+W\mathbf c$ with integers $U,V,W$ form the integer-edge sublattice of that cell; this is the full translation lattice when the chosen basis is primitive. Consider a nonzero vector of this form.

changes.before: this picks the first lattice point met along the ray, i.e. the shortest lattice vector in that direction.
changes.after: this picks the first point of the integer-edge sublattice met along the ray. It is the shortest vector of the full translation lattice on that ray only when the cell basis is primitive; conventional centred cells can have nearer lattice points with fractional cell coordinates.

changes.before: Hence there is no lattice point strictly between the origin and the primitive triple on its ray.
changes.after: Hence no point of the integer-edge sublattice lies strictly between the origin and the coprime triple on its ray. For a primitive lattice basis this also excludes intermediate points of the full lattice. For example, conventional bcc cell indices $[111]$ are coprime, but the body-centre vector $\tfrac12(\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c)$ is halfway along that ray.

changes.before: the green one the shortest vector on its line
changes.after: the green one the shortest integer-edge vector on its ray

changes.before: Here opposite planes $(hkl)$ and $(\bar h\bar k\bar l)$ are counted as different when the group lacks an inversion.
changes.after: Opposite indexed normals $(hkl)$ and $(\bar h\bar k\bar l)$ are retained as distinct orbit members whenever both occur. They may be symmetry related with or without inversion; the stabilizer here fixes the oriented normal, not just its unoriented line.

changes.before: A position may be a fixed point, a line or a plane, with one, two or three free coordinates;
changes.after: A special position may be a fixed point, a line or a plane, with zero, one or two free coordinates respectively; a general position has three free coordinates;
